channel.title: The Kimberley Echo - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Kimberley Echo (kimberleyecho.com.au)

item.title: Film explores healing after Kimberley floods
item.description: A short film exploring cultural healing after the devastating 2023 Kimberley floods has screened in Broome.

item.title: $5 million grant announced for key worker homes in Fitzroy Crossing
item.description: The State Government will spend $5 million to support key worker housing in Fitzroy Crossing.

item.title: WA weather: Authorities issue warning ahead of scorching heatwave set to sizzle through parts of State
item.description: People in parts of the State are set to swelter through intense heat, prompting a fresh warning from authorities.

item.title: Nearly $20m for Kununurra Aboriginal Short Stay Accommodation redirected to social housing
item.description: Nearly $20m in State Government funding initially committed to the Kununurra Aboriginal Short Stay Accommodation project has been redirected to refurbish and build new social homes.

item.title: Community-minded residents encouraged to join Shire of Broome working groups
item.description: The Shire of Brome is calling on community-minded residents to get involved with two of its working groups — the arts and culture reference group and the community safety working group.

item.title: Tyrant’s name to be removed from Kimberley with new name proposed for King Leopold Ranges locality
item.description: A tyrant’s name for an area of the Kimberley may soon be replaced.

item.title: Kimberley on alert for invasive weed praxelis as wet season sets in
item.description: The Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development has urged Kimberley residents to be on the lookout for an invasive weed.

item.title: Derby man charged with meth and cocaine possession on New Year’s Day
item.description: A 26-year-old man from Derby allegedly found with meth and cocaine during a traffic stop on New Year’s Day has been charged with possession.

item.title: Wyndham weather radar to be down for next three months after lightning strike on Christmas Day
item.description: The Wyndham weather radar is expected to be out of action for the next three months after it was struck by lightning on Christmas Day, the Bureau of Meteorology says.

item.title: Lake Argyle Swim gearing up for its biggest year yet in 2026
item.description: The Lake Argyle Swim is gearing up for its biggest year yet, with more than 700 people coming from across the country for the iconic Kimberley event on May 2.
